cim: UH researchers developing AI tool to predict invasive beetle spread
cim_eredeti: UH researchers developing AI tool to predict invasive beetle spread
szoveg_eredeti:
HONOLULU (HawaiiNewsNow) - University of Hawaii researchers are developing an artificial intelligence tool to predict where invasive coconut rhinoceros beetles are most likely to spread across the neighbor islands.

The $300,000 project at UH Manoa’s College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resilience aims to help farmers and response teams identify high-risk areas on Kauai, Maui and Hawaii Island.

Researchers plan to use machine learning to analyze local environmental conditions that allow the beetles to survive and create maps predicting where infestations could spread.

The maps could help field crews determine where to place traps and focus efforts to detect and contain new infestations.

“Knowing where the coconut rhinoceros beetle is likely to spread gives farmers and response teams a major advantage.” said assistant professor Pascal Aigbedion-Atlor, who is leading the project.

”Our technology aims to help farmers and agriculture officials act early, target high-risk areas and protect valuable crops and landscapes," he added.

The project is funded by the Foundation for Food & Agriculture Research, with matching support from UH.

Researchers will test their predictions against field observations to improve the tool’s accuracy.

UH officials said the technology could eventually be adapted to help protect Hawaii crops from other invasive pets.

The university is also working with the state and federal agencies, private organizations and residents to help limit the beetle spread.
